reader.requirement: At --std 85, FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE(argument-1 {argument-2}...) returns an (implementor-precision) approximation of the sum over each argument-2 occurrence k=1..n of argument-2(k) / (1 + argument-1) ** k, for literals, items of any numeric usage, expressions and table(ALL) arguments (ODO included), the rate being any value > -1.

edition-consulted.switches: D8 edition window: sig.IntroducedIn (85 for the 1989 module rows, IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build) against ctx.Edition.DialectLevel; COBOL1502/1503 outside it

ConstructRegistry NumericFunctionIdentifierOperand2002: at 85 a numeric/integer function written where an identifier stands (MOVE sender) is refused (COBOL0900), per §1989:A.2.3 GR2/GR3; never reached inside an arithmetic expression
Edition.DigitCapacityExcess: 18-digit cap on items and literals at 85 (31 later); bounds the argument range only
num.StandardDecimal (OPTIONS ARITHMETIC, a 2002+ paragraph, so always native at 85): the native dispatch is the one a 2023 program with no ARITHMETIC clause takes

reader.edition-search: grep of IntrinsicBinder.cs, IntrinsicRenderer.cs, IntrinsicCarrierRules.cs, FunctionValueLane.cs for Edition|DialectLevel|CobolVersion|ArithmeticMode|StandardDecimal; the runtime bodies take no edition input
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the native exact-list arm (PresentValueExact, then NarrowResult to binary64) is the same at 85 and 2023
reader.witnesses-cover: part: witnesses cover a rate near -1, rate 0 and 0.5 with 18-digit amounts and table(ALL); not multi-period ordinary rates, negative rate, COMP-3 amounts, ODO ALL, expression arguments

probes.printed: COBOL1504 'takes at least 2 argument(s); 1 given'; COBOL1627 for alphanumeric rate and numeric-edited amount

reader.notes: All values match the exact oracle to the receiver's precision. PV(0 -999999999999999999) is computed exactly and then narrowed to binary64 (-1E18), which is 19 digits, so an S9(18) receiver takes a size error. The text leaves the approximation's characteristics to the implementor (§1989:A.2.3 GR2) and a size error without the phrase leaves the receiver undefined (§1985:VI.6.4.2 GR3), so this is within the rule. It is a quality lead: the exact value fits the edition's largest item.
